chunks: And from him, from Salamah, from Ja'far ibn Bashir, from Aban ibn 'Uthman, from Al-Sadusi, from Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: Whoever comes to me as a visitor, I will be his intercessor on the Day of Judgment.
ai.seo_question: What is the reward for visiting the Prophet Muhammad according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Kamil al-Ziyarat* establishes the spiritual merit of visiting the Prophet’s grave, linking physical pilgrimage to the eschatological promise of his intercession (*shafa'ah*). In Shia tradition, this visitation is not merely commemorative but a means of drawing closer to divine grace, with the Prophet acting as the intercessor for those who honor his presence. The narration underscores the enduring bond between the believer and the Prophet, extending beyond his earthly life into the Hereafter.
